plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the agent–environment interaction loop in reinforcement learning, depicted as a closed directed cycle between two rounded rectangular boxes filled with light teal. The upper box is labeled “Agent” with the policy π[a_t | s_t] inscribed inside, and the lower, larger box is labeled “Environment” with the state transition probability Pr(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) inscribed inside. Orange arrows with arrowheads form the loop: one arrow routes from the Agent box rightward and downward into the Environment box, carrying the action a_t; a second arrow returns from the Environment to the Agent carrying the current state s_t, while a third routes the next state s_{t+1} back around; additional arrow paths carry rewards r_t and r_{t+1}, and a label identifies the reward function Pr(r_{t+1} | s_t, a_t). Small white-background rectangles along the arrow paths isolate variable labels — State, Action, and Reward — for readability. This figure introduces the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework at the core of reinforcement learning, showing how the agent observes a state, selects an action according to its policy, and receives a reward and next state from the environment in a repeating closed loop.

interactionPlan.concept: Reinforcement learning is a closed agent-environment loop: the agent observes a state, chooses an action via its policy, and the environment returns a reward and the next state, repeating every time step.

interactions.label: Step one MDP time step
interactions.teaches: Stepping through the phases shows the loop is a strict sequence each step: the state s_t flows into the agent, the agent emits an action a_t, then the environment returns the reward r_{t+1} and next state s_{t+1} — the cycle that repeats forever
The agent's entire role is summarized by its policy π[a_t | s_t]: a mapping from the observed state to a distribution over actions, and the only thing it sends outward is the action a_t

The environment is fully described by two probabilities — the state transition Pr(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) and the reward function Pr(r_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) — both conditioned on the current state and the agent's action

demo_steps.title: The closed loop
demo_steps.narration: Two boxes, Agent and Environment, are joined by orange arrows into a single directed cycle. Everything in reinforcement learning happens inside this repeating loop.

demo_steps.title: 1. Agent observes the state
demo_steps.narration: The environment emits the current state s_t, which travels up into the Agent. The agent's only window onto the world is this state signal.

demo_steps.title: 2. Agent acts via its policy
demo_steps.narration: Using its policy π[a_t | s_t], the agent selects an action a_t and sends it down into the Environment. Click the Agent box to isolate the policy and the outgoing action arrow.

demo_steps.title: 3. Environment responds
demo_steps.narration: Conditioned on (s_t, a_t), the environment draws a reward r_{t+1} and a next state s_{t+1} and returns them, closing the loop and starting the next step. Click the Environment box to highlight the transition and reward functions that produce them.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The agent never sees the environment's internals — its only interface is the loop itself: state in, action out, reward back — so all learning must be extracted from this repeated cycle.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Place the smaller Agent box top-center and the larger Environment box bottom-center, both light teal rounded rectangles with black text. Route orange arrows around the sides to form a clockwise-ish closed cycle: action a_t down the right into Environment; state s_t, next state s_{t+1}, and rewards r_t / r_{t+1} up the left into Agent. Put each variable name (Reward r_t, State s_t, State s_t, Action a_t) in a small white rounded chip sitting on its arrow path for legibility. Draw a short dashed vertical line on the left between the r_t/s_t stream and the r_{t+1}/s_{t+1} stream to mark the time-step boundary. On each loopStep phase, brighten/thicken only the relevant arrow(s) and dim the rest; on agentFocus highlight the policy text and the a_t arrow; on environmentFocus highlight the two probability labels inside the Environment box.

discrepancies: The four edge labels (Reward rₜ, State sₜ, State sₜ, Action aₜ) are wrapped in white rounded-rectangle chips with visible gray borders, whereas the source renders them as plain text sitting directly on the orange arrow paths with no boxed chip.
Inside the Environment box the probability expressions read 'Pr(sₜ₊₁ | sₜ, a)' and 'Pr(rₜ₊₁ | sₜ, a)' using a bare 'a', while the source writes the conditioned action with a subscript as 'aₜ'.
evaluation.notes: The agent–environment MDP loop is faithfully reproduced — correct teal boxes, orange arrow topology and directions, dashed time-step separator with sₜ₊₁/r₊₁, and a working 4-step demo player that highlights the observe/act/reward phases — with only minor deviations: boxed label chips not present in the source and a missing subscript on the conditioned action 'a'.
action_items: Drop the gray-bordered white rounded-rect chips around the four edge labels (Reward rₜ, State sₜ, State sₜ, Action aₜ) and instead use a borderless white text halo/mask so they read as plain labels on the arrow lines, matching the source.
Replace the bare 'a' with 'aₜ' in both Environment-box expressions 'Pr(sₜ₊₁ | sₜ, aₜ)' and 'Pr(rₜ₊₁ | sₜ, aₜ)' to match the source notation.

Strengthen the loop-step phase feedback (e.g. animate a small token traveling along the active arrow or use a clearer color/width change) so the observe→act→reward cycle is more visually obvious than a subtle opacity/width dim.

feedback.rationale: Scores are consistently high (4–5), no failure modes are listed, and the remaining discrepancies are trivial cosmetic details (label chip styling and a missing subscript) that do not meaningfully affect comprehension or usability.
